title: Control plane API as a material
goal: Define the control plane's own API in TypeSpec so the factory builds its own product.
acceptance: `materials/control-plane-api/` defines resources for materials, material versions, products, product builds, runs, run steps, gate results and waivers
Spectral and oasdiff pass; Angular client and NestJS server packages are released to Verdaccio
docs/architecture.md links the resource model to the control plane modules

title: control-plane-api service with catalog endpoints
goal: The backend for the catalog, reading from the material graph.
acceptance: `products/control-plane-api` is assembled with the nestjs-service recipe and implements the generated controllers
Catalog endpoints list and search materials, versions, owners, states and consuming products, backed by the graph service
Pagination and filtering are covered by tests; contract tests pass against the generated client

title: Recipe: angular-shell with Native Federation
goal: A golden-path host that loads remotes from a manifest.
acceptance: `recipes/angular-shell` generates a standalone Angular host using Native Federation with a remote manifest, layout, navigation and error boundary per remote
A remote that fails to load shows an error panel and does not break the shell (test proves it)
Generated shell passes lint, test and build

title: Control plane shell with Keycloak sign-in
goal: One app that hosts every control plane module behind SSO.
acceptance: `products/control-plane-shell` is assembled from the angular-shell recipe
Sign-in uses Keycloak via OIDC (docker compose realm export checked in, no real secrets)
Routes are guarded; the API rejects unauthenticated calls
Playwright test signs in with a test user and reaches the home page

title: Catalog remote
acceptance: `products/catalog-remote` (angular-remote) lists materials and products with search, filters by type, owner and state, and a detail page with versions and consumers
Uses only the generated control-plane-api client
Playwright test covers search and detail navigation; axe-core finds no serious accessibility issues

title: Run orchestrator with Temporal: spec-change workflow
goal: Turn Flow B into a durable, observable workflow.
acceptance: `products/run-orchestrator` (nestjs-service) runs a Temporal worker; Temporal dev server added to docker compose
Workflow `specChange` runs validate, impact, release and propagation as activities that call the existing factory CLI
Each step's status and evidence are written through the control-plane-api runs endpoints
Temporal test environment covers success, a failed validation, and retry of a flaky step

title: Run control room remote
goal: A live view of every run: steps, evidence and approvals.
acceptance: `products/runs-remote` lists active and recent runs and shows a run's steps updating live over server-sent events
Each step shows its evidence links; failed steps show the error
A run waiting for approval shows Approve and Reject buttons that call the API (approval recorded with the user)
Playwright test drives a fake run from start to finish

title: Gate center: gate results ingestion and UI
goal: One place that shows why the line stopped.
acceptance: `POST /gate-results` accepts verdicts with evidence from CI (authenticated with a CI token)
Dagger gate blocks post their results after each run
`products/gates-remote` shows results per product and PR, and lets an authorised user add a waiver with expiry and reason
Expired waivers stop applying (test proves it)

title: Product studio: create a product from a recipe
goal: Flow A starts with a form, not a terminal.
acceptance: Each recipe publishes a JSON Schema for its product.yaml options
`products/product-studio-remote` renders the form with Formly, validates it, and on submit opens a PR adding `products/<name>/product.yaml`
The PR triggers assembly through the run orchestrator
Playwright test fills the form and asserts the PR payload (GitHub API mocked)

title: Material studio: edit specs with live validation
goal: Edit a material and see its effects before opening a PR.
acceptance: `products/material-studio-remote` opens a material's TypeSpec source in Monaco
Edits are validated live (TypeSpec compile plus Spectral) through an API endpoint; errors show inline
A preview tab shows the emitted OpenAPI and the generated Angular client for the edited source
Save opens a PR; the impact report from P2-06 appears on it

title: Event bus: NATS for factory events
goal: Bays talk through events instead of direct calls.
acceptance: NATS JetStream added to docker compose and the platform charts
Events `spec.changed`, `material.released`, `gate.result`, `image.pushed`, `material.recalled` have AsyncAPI definitions as a material
The registry hook, CI gate blocks and recall command publish events; the orchestrator subscribes and starts workflows
Integration test publishes `spec.changed` and observes a `specChange` workflow start

title: Package the control plane: Helm chart and one-command dev stack
goal: A design partner can install it.
acceptance: `deploy/charts/control-plane` installs every control plane service and remote using factory-lib
`scripts/dev-up.sh` starts the full stack locally with docker compose and seeds demo data
Install on the kind cluster from P2-10 passes a smoke test of sign-in, catalog and a run
docs/install.md covers prerequisites, install, upgrade and uninstall

title: Gate 3 package: design-partner onboarding
goal: Everything a design partner needs to run Flow A without us.
acceptance: docs/design-partner.md walks through install, connecting a Git host, creating a first product and reading a run
A seeded demo organisation shows each module with realistic data
A recorded checklist run of Flow A on a fresh install passes
PROGRESS.md records the evidence and the planner opens `Gate 3 review` for a human
